previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and recent cholangitis was admitted for fever and altered mental status. He had been experiencing fatigue, imbalance, and worsening leg edema at home. Initial evaluation revealed bibasilar lung opacities on chest X-ray suggestive of pneumonia, though he lacked respiratory symptoms. A CT head showed no acute intracranial process, and blood and urine cultures were negative. He was treated with IV antibiotics, but due to lost IV access, was transitioned to oral cefpodoxime and azithromycin. His mental status improved rapidly, and he remained afebrile for over 24 hours prior to discharge. His sirolimus level was elevated at 12.6, prompting a dose reduction to 1.5 mg daily. Lower extremity edema, likely related to sirolimus, was managed with compression stockings. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete his antibiotic course and follow up at the transplant clinic for repeat sirolimus level monitoring.
